facts.text: The opening titles are in French, and the producer is credited as "Guillaume Osco" — that's Bill Osco, husband of director Jackie Kong at the time, who also produced her earlier film The Being.
Murray Langston's "Unknown Comic" act, a comedian in a paper bag, came from TV's The Gong Show. Night Patrol was a vehicle built around him; it was even announced as "The Unknown Comic Movie."
Murray Langston (The Unknown Comic) said he put a bag on his head for The Gong Show so nobody would know he'd been on Sonny & Cher. "I had a really bad complexion, and it was cheaper than Clearasil."
Linda Blair has said Night Patrol was no Police Academy cash-in. Murray Langston wrote the script before Police Academy existed, but rewrites and production problems delayed the film until after it.
Before the bag, Murray Langston got on Laugh-In by phoning the show and offering an impression of a fork. He was booked four times as "downtown Burbank's greatest impressionist."
Linda Blair (Officer Sue Perman) won the 1985 Razzie for Worst Actress, awarded for this film plus Savage Island and Savage Streets, all in one year.
Murray Langston once ran a North Hollywood club, Showbiz, where future stars David Letterman and Debra Winger worked early on. He joked it "specialized in ribs and later specialized in bankruptcy."
Billy Barty (Captain Lewis) was furious when director Jackie Kong added flatulence sound effects in post-production to make his character seem to fart constantly. He reportedly tried to sue.
Billy Barty founded Little People of America in 1957 and was 3 ft 9 in tall. Here he plays Captain Lewis, a pathological liar.
Linda Blair said in a 1999 interview that Jackie Kong wasn't "playing with a full deck." She claimed Kong demanded needless retakes of Murray Langston and that he eventually quit the project.
Director Jackie Kong's Night Patrol was a comeback of sorts: the New York Times' Vincent Canby praised its "good, low-burlesque style," though he called the humor strictly for the stag-party crowd.
Director Jackie Kong's own website says the Recording Industry Association of America gave her a Platinum Video Award for Night Patrol, which became a college-party staple on tape.
TV Guide said the film "does the impossible: It makes Police Academy look like a piece of sophisticated humor." The Chicago Tribune's Richard Christiansen said it seemed made by "subnormal persons."
Disc jockey Machine Gun Kelly pops up in the cast. He also appeared in Linda Blair's earlier Roller Boogie (1979) and in Voyage of the Rock Aliens.
Andrew Dice Clay is in this movie as stand-up Tony Baroni, billed as "Andy Clay". It was one of his earliest film roles, years before his Dice Man stardom.
Murray Langston later produced Playboy TV's The Unknown Comedy Hour, then The Sex and Violence Family Hour, which starred a very young Jim Carrey.
Pat Morita, soon to be Mr. Miyagi in The Karate Kid (1984), has a bit part here as a crime victim.
Night Patrol became late-night cable filler: it aired several times on USA Network's Up All Night between 1989 and 1992.
Pat Paulsen (Officer Kent Lane) ran for U.S. President as a satirical candidate starting in 1968 and kept at it until 1996. In 1967–68 he won an Emmy for The Smothers Brothers Comedy Hour.
Jack Riley, who plays shrink Dr. Ziegler, was famous as the miserable patient Elliot Carlin on The Bob Newhart Show, and later voiced Stu Pickles in Rugrats.
Sydney Lassick, Charlie Cheswick in One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest, plays a peeping tom. Reginald VelJohnson (later Die Hard and Family Matters) is also among the cops.
Jaye P. Morgan (agent Kate Parker) was a 1950s hit singer. She was a Gong Show panelist famous for baring her breasts on air, which got her fired from the show.
Murray Langston and Jaye P. Morgan were both Gong Show regulars. They also appeared together in The Gong Show Movie (1980) and Confessions of a Dangerous Mind (2002).
Linda Blair and Murray Langston made two films together: Night Patrol and the romantic comedy Up Your Alley.
The film's reported budget of $4.5 million dates from a 1981 Variety item, long before the shoot reportedly went to weekends only with the cast on deferred pay.
Night Patrol grossed $8,165,432 in its run. Its first week in New York earned $776,218 across 94 theaters.
The restaurant scenes were shot at Rae's Restaurant on Pico Boulevard in Santa Monica. Other locations include Venice jail, MacArthur Park and the Comedy & Magic Club in Hermosa Beach.
The film opened regionally in Dallas on November 20, 1984. Los Angeles got it January 4, 1985, and New York March 8, 1985, by AFI's count.
Jackie Kong on Night Patrol: "I did that with no money." She says NYT critic Vincent Canby wrote that it "made me laugh even though I didn't want to."
Jackie Kong did the directing, editing, co-writing and co-producing on this film, then got a three-picture Vestron deal. Vestron folded after Blood Diner and The Under Achievers (both 1987).
Night Patrol is one of many 1980s cop spoofs after Police Academy (1984), alongside Feds, Recruits, Off Beat, Moving Violations and Hollywood Vice Squad.
The film shoots at E.T.: it spoofs E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial (1982) and also references Saturday Night Fever and Welcome Back, Kotter.
In 1985 New World Video released an unrated cut on tape with about two minutes of footage not in the R-rated theatrical version.
Night Patrol is name-checked in Kong's later cult gore comedy Blood Diner (1987). Kong's best-known film, it eventually got a Vestron Video Collector's Series Blu-ray.
Another 1984 film is also called Night Patrol: the French film Ronde de nuit. IMDb notes the confusion.
A blog review at The Retro Network scored Night Patrol 3/10, saying it needs a plot and repeats "the same 10-12 jokes" after the first 30-40 minutes.
A Blu-ray from Scorpion Releasing arrived January 14, 2020, 35 years after release.
Pat Paulsen's Kent Lane flubs his line here: IMDb lists a goof where he speaks too early, interrupting Jack Riley's Dr. Zeigler after the gun duel.
